text:
A charged particle (mass m and charge q)

moves along X-axis with velocity $V_{0}$. When it

passes through the origin it enters a region
having uniform electric field 

$\vec{E}=-E\hat{j}$ which
extends upto x = d. 
Equation of path of electron
in the region x > d is

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let particle have charge q and mass 'm

We know, $F = ma_{y} = qE$

$\therefore$ $a_{y}=\frac{qE}{m}$

As electric field is along vertical direction so horizontal component of acceleration is zero.

$\therefore$ $a_{x} = 0$

Applying, $S=u_{y}t+\frac{1}{2}a_{y}t^{2}$

$-y=0\times t+\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{qE}{m}\right )t^{2}$ ....(1)

Also, $x=V_{0}t$

$\Rightarrow t=\frac{x}{V_{0}}$

Putting in (1) we get,

$y=-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{qE}{m}\right )\left (\frac{x}{V_{0}}\right )^{2}$

Differentiating with respect to x, 

$\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{qE}{m}\left (\frac{x}{V_{0}^{2}}\right )$

$\therefore$ Slope = $m=\tan θ=-\frac{qE}{m}\left (\frac{x}{V_{0}^{2}}\right )$

when x = d, then $m=-\frac{qE}{m}\left (\frac{d}{V_{0}^{2}}\right )$

We know, equation of straight line whose slope is m,

y = mx + c

Here m = $\left (-\frac{qEd}{mV_{0}^{2}}\right )$,

$\therefore$ $-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{qE}{m}\right )\left (\frac{d}{V_{0}}\right )^{2}=\left (-\frac{qEd}{mV_{0}^{2}}\right )d+c$

$\Rightarrow$ c = $\frac{qEd}{2mV_{0}^{2}}$

Putting the value of c, we get

$y=-\left (\frac{qEd}{mV_{0}^{2}}\right )x+\frac{qEd^{2}}{2mV_{0}^{2}}$

$=\frac{qEd}{mV_{0}^{2}}\left (\frac{d}{2}-x\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot

text:
The mass density of a spherical galaxy varies
as
$\frac{K}{r}$ over a large distance ‘r’ from its centre.
In that region, a small star is in a circular orbit
of radius R. Then the period of revolution, T
depends on R as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


dm = $ρ$dv

$\Rightarrow$ dm = $\left (\frac{k}{r}\right )$ (4$πr^{2}dr)$

$\Rightarrow$ dm = 4$π$krdr

M = $\int\limits _{0}^{R}dm$ = $\int\limits _{0}^{R}4πkrdr$

$\Rightarrow$ M = $4πk\left [\frac{r^{2}}{2}\right ]_{0}^{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ M = 2$πkR^{2}$

 For circular motion gravitational force will provide required centripetal force.

 $\frac{GMm}{R^{2}}$ = $\frac{mv^{2}}{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{G\left (2πkR^{2}\right )m}{R^{2}}$ = $\frac{mv^{2}}{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ v = $\sqrt{2πGkR}$

 Time period, T = $\frac{2πR}{v}$

= $\frac{2πR}{\sqrt{2πGkR}}$ $\propto$ $\sqrt{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $T^{2}$ $\propto$ R

text:
A particle of mass m with an initial velocity $u\hat{i}$
collides perfectly elastically with a mass 3 m at
rest. It moves with a velocity $v\hat{j}$ after collision,
then, v is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


From momentum conservation

m(u)$\hat{i}$ + 3m(0) = mv$\hat{j}$ + 3m$\vec{v^{'}}$

$\Rightarrow$ 3m$\vec{v^{'}}$ = m(u)$\hat{i}$ - mv$\hat{j}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{v^{'}}=\frac{u\hat{i}-v\hat{j}}{3}$

$\therefore$ $\left |\vec{v^{'}}\right |=\frac{\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left |\vec{v^{'}}\right |^{2}=\frac{u^{2}+v^{2}}{9}$ ......(1)

As collision is perfectly elastic hence 

$KE_{i}$
 $= KE_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}+\frac{1}{2}(3m)\times 0^{2}=\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}+\frac{1}{2}3m(v^{'})^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $u^{2} = v^{2} + 3(v^{'})^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $u^{2} = v^{2} + 3\left (\frac{u^{2}+v^{2}}{9}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $3u^{2} = 3v^{2} + u^{2} + v^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $2u^{2} = 4v^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v=\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot

text:
In a reactor, 2 kg of $_{92}U^{235}$ fuel is fully used up
in 30 days. The energy released per fission is
200 MeV. Given that the Avogadro number,
N = 6.023 $\times$ $10^{26}$ per kilo mole and 1 eV =
$1.6 × 10^{–19} J$. The power output of the reactor is
close to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Number of uranium atoms in 2 kg

= $\frac{2\times 6.023\times 10^{26}}{235}$

Energy from one atom is $200 × 10^{6}$
e.V. hence total energy from 2 kg uranium

= $\frac{2\times 6.023\times 10^{26}}{235}\times 200\times 10^{6}$ eV

= $\frac{2\times 6.023\times 10^{26}}{235}\times 200\times 10^{6}$ $\times$ $1.6 × 10^{–19} J$

2 kg uranium is used in 30 days  hence energy received per second or
power is 

Power = $\frac{2\times 6.023\times 10^{26}\times 200\times 10^{6}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}}{235\times 30\times 24\times 3600}$

$= 63.2 × 10^{6}$ watt or 63.2 Mega Watt

$\simeq$ 60 MW

text:
An engine takes in 5 moles of air at $20^{o}C$ and
1 atm, and compresses it adiabatically to
$1/10^{th}$ of the original volume. Assuming air to
be a diatomic ideal gas made up of rigid
molecules, the change in its internal energy
during this process comes out to be X kJ. The
value of X to the nearest integer $is________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For diatomic ideal gas :

f = 5

$γ$ = $\frac{7}{5}$

$T_{i}$
 = T = 273 + 20 = 293 K

$V_{i}$
 = V

$V_{f} =$ $\frac{V}{10}$

For adiabatic process $TV^{γ - 1} =$ constant

$T_{1}V_{1}^{γ-1}=T_{2}V_{2}^{γ-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(293)V^{\frac{7}{5}-1}=T_{2}\left (\frac{V}{10}\right )^{\frac{7}{5}-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $T_{2}=293\times (10)^{\frac{2}{5}}$

$\Delta$U = $\frac{nfR(T_{2}-T_{1})}{2}$

= $\frac{5\times 5\times \frac{25}{3}\times \left (293.10^{\dfrac{2}{5}}-293\right )}{2}$

= $\frac{625\times 293\times \left (10^{\dfrac{2}{5}}-1\right )}{6}$

= 46.14 $\times$ $10^{3} J$

$\simeq$ 46 kJ

text:
When radiation of wavelength $λ$ is used to
illuminate a metallic surface, the stopping
potential is V. When the same surface is
illuminated with radiation of wavelength 3$λ$,
the stopping potential is
$\frac{V}{4}$. If the threshold
wavelength for the metallic surface is n$λ$ then
value of n will be $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{hc}{λ}-𝜙$ = eV .....(i)

$\frac{hc}{3λ}-𝜙=\frac{eV}{4}$ .....(ii)

From (i) and (ii),

$\frac{hc}{3λ}-𝜙=$ $\frac{hc}{4λ}-\frac{𝜙}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{hc}{λ}\left (\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}\right )=\frac{3𝜙}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{hc}{9λ}=𝜙$

Also, $𝜙$ = $\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{hc}{9λ}=\frac{hc}{λ_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $𝜙$ = 9$λ$

So, n = 9
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot
